title: Staged activation resource map + KPI lab notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook to coordinate a staged activation (multi-phase rollout) for product features with a focus on: resource allocation, KPI observability, and gating decisions. Use this doc during dry-run rehearsals and the first 72 hours of live traffic.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to medium-to-large feature launches (expected 10k-200k daily requests).
- Primary metrics to protect: latency p50/p95, error-rate, user success rate (UCR), cost per active request.
- Environment: hosted + dedicated hybrid deployments (Redwood Dedicated fallback path available).
- Goal: predictable ramp with clear rollback gates and minimal manual firefighting.

High-level activation phases (staged):
1) Canary smoke (0.1% traffic, 30 min): verify end-to-end happy path, top-5 integration points.
2) Micro-ramp (1% traffic, 2 hours): observe load behavior on batching, cache hit rates.
3) Controlled ramp (10% traffic, 6-12 hours): monitor upstream services and cost signals.
4) Broad ramp (50% traffic, 24 hours): readiness for full load tests.
5) Full traffic (100% traffic): post-rollout validation and stabilization.

Roles & primary contacts (on-call shift order):
- Launch lead: Marisol Vega (product-ops)
- SRE lead: Evan Brooks
- Serving runtime owner: Priya Nair
- Observability & alerts: Diego Morales
- Customer success triage: Ruth Chen
- Exec escalation: Jonah Park (on-call exec)

Resource map (what to allocate for each phase):
- Canary smoke: 1 engineer (runtime), 1 SRE, 1 observations lead — reserve 1 small Dedicated unit for deterministic tests.
- Micro-ramp: +1 runtime eng, +1 infra on-call, enable prefix caching for high-volume prompts.
- Controlled ramp: add autoscale policy to aggressive, open burst capacity to 2x baseline, prioritize KV cache warmup window.
- Broad ramp: coordinate with Dedicated pool owners to ensure headroom, schedule 1-hour cooldown windows every 6 hours.
- Full traffic: runbook handed back to SRE ops; product-ops transitions to monitoring and stakeholding.

KPI definitions & thresholds (watchlist):
- Latency p50: median response time in ms (goal < 120ms at all phases).
- Latency p95: 95th percentile (soft threshold < 350ms; hard threshold 600ms -> trigger rollback).
- Error-rate: non-2xx responses / total requests (soft threshold 0.8% -> investigation; hard >2% -> rollback).
- UCR (user success rate): fraction of responses that meet acceptance criteria from eval set (goal > 97%).
- Token cost per 1k requests: cost signal (trend-based, alert if +30% over projected).
- Cache hit ratio: prefix/KV cache ratio (goal > 60% by Controlled ramp).
- Throughput (rps): match expected baseline +/- 15%.

Gate rules (go/no-go checklist for phase transition):
- No critical errors in last 15 minutes (error-rate < 0.5%).
- p95 below phase-specific threshold (controlled < 400ms).
- Observability signals green: logs flowing, traces sampled, dashboards rendering.
- Cache warmup achieved: prefix cache hit > 40% for micro->controlled.
- Incident backlog: zero P0s and no unresolved latency regressions > 20% from baseline.
- Stakeholder sign-off: product-ops and SRE lead both acknowledge readiness.

Automated fallbacks (pre-configured):
- Traffic auto-throttle: reduce to previous phase if p95 spikes > 40% over 10m window.
- Model variant fallback: route to lighter quantized variant if CPU/GPU queue depth exceeded threshold.
- Region failover: ingress reroute to secondary region when regional latency > 2x baseline and error-rate > 1.5%.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Hard error-rate trigger: >=2% sustained for 10 minutes -> immediate rollback to prior phase.
- Latency hard trigger: p95 >= 600ms sustained for 5 minutes with growing trend -> rollback.
- Functional failure: key endpoint return codes indicating major downstream outage -> rollback and page owners.

Post-rollout 72-hour horizon actions:
- 0-6h: confirm telemetry fidelity, ensure anomaly detectors enabled, maintain high-frequency check-ins (every 30m).
- 6-24h: transition to regular cadence (hourly check-ins).
- 24-72h: confirm KPIs stable, prepare adoption comms and debrief notes.

Runbook snippets (copy to SRE pager):
- Quick rollback CLI: infra traffic-shaper revert --to-phase micro-ramp --reason "p95 regression"
- Increase cache TTLs: runtime-admin set-cache-ttl --key-prefix prompt-* --ttl 900
- Enable limited burst: infra scale-policy apply --pool dedicated-x --multiplier 2

Monitoring dashboard checklist (must exist before go):
- Real-time p50/p95 panel (1m/5m windows)
- Error-rate by endpoint and by client (1m resolution)
- Cache hit ratio and evictions time-series
- Cost delta heatmap (tokens & infra) by route
- Top 10 slow traces and their span breakdown
- Synthetic eval harness scoreboard (permanent 1-min cadence)

Communications plan (who says what):
- T-1h: Launch lead posts rollout plan in #prod-ops with links and SLAs.
- Phase transitions: Launch lead posts phase start and phase end summaries into the thread.
- Any gate failure: SRE lead posts incident stub, pages escalation path.
- Exec summary: 6h & 24h updates to #exec-ops with top-3 risks and mitigation.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated pool warm-start timing with infra team (JIRA: POPS-1293)
- [ ] Add synthetic queries for long-tail prompts to eval harness (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Validate cost projections with finance for burst capacity assumptions (owner: Marisol)
- [ ] Run dry-run rehearsal on staging with simulated traffic window (target: 2024-11-21)

Playbook appendices (quick links):
- Baseline metrics sheet: sheet:activation-capacity-2025
- Postmortem template: confluence:postmortem-template-2
- Rollout CLI docs: github:infra/traffic-shaper#512

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a mid-ramp dark traffic mirror to validate expensive codepaths without user exposure.
- Investigate pre-warming KV files using a small background job to boost cache% before micro-ramp.
- Add a short checklist for CS to capture user-impacting incidents (template snippet included in the CS runbook).

End of notebook. Keep this doc as the canonical scratchpad for the first activation. Move final checklists & metrics to the activation-capacity sheet once validated.
